title: Panchavati
hook: on the road to a new home, a giant bird lands in front of them and says he knew their father

segments.voice: Yesterday: Agastya's weapons, part two. The sage who digested a demon gave Rama Vishnu's bow, and told him to go to Panchavati. Did you use a strength for someone else? Day five hundred fifty-nine.

Halfway there, a huge bird settles on a tree in front of them. A vulture, enormous, old. Rama's first thought, after Viradha, is that it's a rakshasa in disguise, and he asks it who it is. The bird answers gently. I was a friend of your father, he says. My name is Jatayu. And he offers something no one else has. When you two brothers go out into the forest, I'll stay and watch over Sita.
screen: `A GIANT BIRD ON A TREE.` → `I WAS YOUR FATHER'S FRIEND.` → `I'LL WATCH OVER SITA.`

segments.voice: Jatayu, the vulture king, gives his lineage, a long one going back to the beginning of creatures, and Rama, hearing that he was Dasharatha's friend, embraces him. It's a brief meeting, but hold it. Of everyone in the forest book, this old bird's promise to guard Sita will be the one that costs the most. Then they come to Panchavati. The name is usually explained as the place of five banyan trees. It's on the Godavari, with flowering trees, deer, peacocks, and mountains in the distance. Rama turns to Lakshmana and says: you choose the spot. And Lakshmana answers that he'd rather be told. As long as you live, he says, I'm here to do what you ask. So Rama chooses, a level place near the water. And Lakshmana builds the hut. Valmiki describes it with pleasure: walls of packed earth, posts of bamboo, a roof of leaves and long grass, a floor made smooth. Then Lakshmana goes to the river, bathes, gathers flowers and fruit, and makes an offering for the new home. When Rama sees it, he's moved. He holds his brother and says something close to this: with you here, it's as if our father is not gone. That's the heart of Panchavati. Not the scenery, though it's lovely. A brother who builds a house with his own hands, so the family can have a place to live again.
screen: `JATAYU, THE VULTURE KING.` · `PANCHAVATI: FIVE BANYANS.` · `YOU CHOOSE. NO, YOU TELL ME.` · `LAKSHMANA BUILDS THE HUT.` · then, large: `WITH YOU, OUR FATHER IS NOT GONE.`

segments.voice: Sit and feel the room or place around you. Notice one thing in it that someone made or fixed with their hands: a chair, a shelf, a wall, a meal on the stove. Wonder for a moment about who did it. Then think of someone who has built something for you, literally or not, a place to land. Let their face come. Breathe in thanks. Breathe out ease. The bell holds the time.
Panchavati. Five banyans by the Godavari, where Lakshmana builds a hut and Rama says: with you here, our father is not gone.
Your line: Panchavati. Today, make one corner of your home a little better for someone you live with. Day five hundred fifty-nine.

howItsDone: Panchavati is identified by many pilgrims with a site at Nashik on the Godavari, and the hut Lakshmana builds is a favorite scene in Ramayana art and performance.

original.note: Sanskrit jaṭāyu: the old vulture king, friend of Dasharatha, who promises to guard Sita.

trapdoor: what you thought: Panchavati is just a pretty place by a river.
what it means: it's where the brothers make a home again, and Jatayu promises to guard it.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 14–15 pair Jatayu's promise with the hut-building; both matter for what comes next.
